subject: openstack-cli container is 384MB: concurrent python CLI invocations stall each other into multi-minute hangs (solo ~3s). Affects any grader or lab that execs the CLI while a student runs one. Options: raise memory for write-mode labs, or grade via raw REST (token+curl ~40x lighter). Found during Stage 3 e2e 2026-07-30.
description:
[2026-08-01 04:23] MEASURED 2026-08-01, on a real openstack-cli container launched through the normal API path. THE STALL IS CPU-BOUND, NOT MEMORY-BOUND.
  solo, ONE openstack call    4,766 ms
  4 concurrent, wall         24,303 ms   (~5x)
  CPU during                 51.30 51.41 49.50 49.72 49.71 49.82 49.66 %   <- PINNED at the cpus:0.5 cap
  MEM during                 34 -> 235 MiB of 384 MiB peak (61%)           <- never near the limit
  OOM kills                  none
So this ticket's own suggested option 'raise memory for write-mode labs' would spend RAM across every container in the fleet and fix NOTHING. The container definition is server.js:171-182 -- memory 384MB, cpus 0.5, pidsLimit 256. Half a core is the ceiling being hit.
SECOND FINDING, arguably bigger: 4.8 SECONDS PER CALL SOLO. Every openstack CLI invocation is a fresh Python process importing the whole SDK. Anything that needs several calls -- a grader, or a student tool covering multiple resource classes -- pays that per call. Five calls is ~24s with ZERO contention.
OPTIONS, none measured: raise cpus for this image (honest fix if the box stays CLI-based); move to raw REST (token + HTTP, which collapses five 4.8s process starts into one auth plus five requests, and is this ticket's other recommendation); or accept long operations with progress feedback.
NOT MEASURED: this was 4 IDENTICAL concurrent invocations, not the real mixed shape (a grader sequence contending with human-paced terminal use). Establishes the resource dimension and per-call cost; does not establish the worst case.

notes.text:
MEASURED AGAIN 2026-08-01, this time comparing approaches rather than just diagnosing. Same container, back to back:
    CLI, 5 sequential calls (5 fresh Python processes)   19,485 ms
    ONE python process, 1 auth + 5 REST calls               816 ms   (auth 172 + calls 644), 5/5 OK
Verified by PAYLOAD not just clock: volumes 0, servers 0, security-groups 1, networks 3, routers 0 -- real collections returned. Stated because my first attempt measured 392ms and was 392ms of CRASHING (OS_AUTH_URL empty -- this container gets credentials from /etc/openstack/clouds.yaml, NOT env vars). A fast failure and a fast success look identical on a stopwatch.
SO THE 4.8s IS PROCESS SPAWN + SDK IMPORT, NOT API LATENCY. Real round trip is ~130ms/call. The CLI pays a ~4s tax five times to do 644ms of work. That means 'raise cpus' tunes the constant on an approach that is 24x worse -- withdrawn as a fix.
SECOND PROPERTY WORTH KNOWING FOR ANY FUTURE TOOL: the container CANNOT use the Keystone service catalog. It returns bc2-internal 192.168.122.x addresses with no route from the container. clouds.yaml carries explicit per-service ENDPOINT OVERRIDES pointing at the tailscale bridge (100.125.36.2:8080) and those must be used. My code used the catalog and got 404s.
MIDDLE OPTION, unmeasured: one process importing openstacksdk ONCE pays the ~4s import a single time instead of five -- roughly 5s vs 19.5s, with zero new auth concepts since the SDK reads the same clouds.yaml the CLI already uses.

SDK PATH MEASURED 2026-08-01, same container, back to back with the CLI:
    CLI, 5 sequential calls (5 processes)   19,363 ms
    openstacksdk, ONE process                2,321 ms   (import 1,299 + connect 240 + 5 calls 782), 5/5 OK
    raw REST, ONE process                      816 ms   (measured earlier), 5/5 OK
THE SDK HONORS THE clouds.yaml ENDPOINT OVERRIDES -- counts identical to the REST run (0,0,1,3,0), no catalog fallback, no 404s. That was the unverified assumption Nancy refused to let through, and it is the same shape as the two false reads earlier tonight.
CORRECTION to my own earlier estimate: I guessed the SDK import was the ~4s cost. It is 1.3s. The CLI's extra weight is its cliff/stevedore plugin-loading wrapper sitting ON TOP of the same SDK -- the CLI pays for machinery a tool does not need.
CONCLUSION for #248 generally, beyond this one project: ANY multi-call tooling on this box should connect once via openstacksdk rather than shelling out to the openstack binary per call. That is an 8x win with zero new concepts and it applies to graders as much as to student tools.
